To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ROUGE 1 is the best automatic evaluation metric for summarization of news and ROUGE 2 is the best automatic metric for evaluating the content quality of summaries.
ROUGE 1 is the best measure for evaluating the content of a system and ROUGE 2 is the best measure of the content and order of a system.
ROUGE 2 is the most accurate of the metrics that have been used in the TAC 2008 and 2009 summarization tasks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: what are the best automatic evaluation metrics to use for summarization research, and how can they be used correctly?
understanding the accuracy of automatic evaluation and the proper use of automatic evaluation in summarization.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ROUGE-1 and ROUGE-2 metrics, when used correctly, can be used to reliably identify the statistically significant differences between two systems, and can be used as an accurate surrogate to the manual evaluation process.

the ROUGE-2 F-score is the most accurate of the reference automatic evaluation measures, and that it can be used to find systems which are significantly better than other systems in the content of the generated summaries.
the use of the ROUGE 1, 2 and L metrics is justified, as they are sufficiently accurate and reliable to support system comparisons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the automatic evaluation metrics are not a panacea.
the reference evaluation is accurate, but it is not perfect.
automatic evaluation is a very useful tool, but its accuracy and limitations need to be understood and respected.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of automatic evaluations in summarization should not be taken for granted.
automatic evaluations are not only useful, but can be accurate, if used correctly.
the ROUGE 1, 2 metrics are accurate enough to be used to find significant differences between systems, and to identify the most promising new metrics.
